title: Diplomatic Disagreement
completion_message: ¡Soberbio! Decir 'no' en el mundo corporativo es un arte. Has aprendido a desarmar la oposición con elegancia, firmeza y profesionalismo diplomático.

parts.visual:
En reuniones C2, nunca decimos 'You're wrong'. Usamos lenguaje diplomático para rechazar ideas sin ofender. 

1. With all due respect (Con el debido respeto): 
- La frase clásica para introducir un desacuerdo fuerte. 
Ej: WITH ALL DUE RESPECT, I don't think that strategy will work. 

2. I beg to differ (Me permito discrepar): 
- Una forma extremadamente educada y formal de decir 'no estoy de acuerdo'. 
Ej: You said profits are up, but looking at the data, I BEG TO DIFFER. 

3. That's a valid point, but... (Es un punto válido, pero...): 
- La técnica del 'Yes, but'. Valida a la persona antes de destruirla con lógica. 
Ej: THAT'S A VALID POINT, BUT we don't have the budget for it.
parts.audio: Welcome to Diplomatic Disagreement. In a C2 level meeting, we never simply say 'You are wrong'. That is aggressive and unprofessional. We use diplomatic language to push back. Number 1: With all due respect. The classic phrase to introduce a strong disagreement politely. For example: WITH ALL DUE RESPECT, I don't think that strategy will work. Number 2: I beg to differ. An extremely polite, highly formal way to say 'I disagree'. For example: You said profits are up, but looking at the data, I BEG TO DIFFER. Number 3: That's a valid point, but... This is the 'Yes, but' technique. You validate the person before destroying their argument with logic. For example: THAT'S A VALID POINT, BUT we don't have the budget for it.

parts.visual:
4. I have reservations about... (Tengo reservas/dudas sobre...): 
- Una forma suave de expresar preocupación o rechazo. 
Ej: I HAVE SERIOUS RESERVATIONS ABOUT partnering with them. 

5. Let's agree to disagree (Acordemos no estar de acuerdo): 
- Cuando es imposible convencer al otro y quieres cerrar el tema pacíficamente. 
Ej: We're not making progress. LET'S AGREE TO DISAGREE and move on. 

6. To play devil's advocate (Ser el abogado del diablo): 
- Discutir en contra de una idea solo para probar su fortaleza. 
Ej: TO PLAY DEVIL'S ADVOCATE, what happens if the server crashes? 

7. Pushback (Resistencia / Rechazo): 
- Sustantivo para describir cuando la gente se opone a tu idea. 
Ej: Be prepared to get a lot of PUSHBACK from the board.
parts.audio: Number 4: I have reservations about... A soft, professional way to express concern or rejection. For example: I HAVE SERIOUS RESERVATIONS ABOUT partnering with them. Number 5: Let's agree to disagree. When it's impossible to convince the other person and you want to close the topic peacefully. For example: We're not making progress. LET'S AGREE TO DISAGREE and move on. Number 6: To play devil's advocate. To argue against an idea simply to test its strength. For example: TO PLAY DEVIL'S ADVOCATE, what happens if the server crashes? Finally, Number 7: Pushback. A noun used to describe resistance or opposition to an idea. For example: Be prepared to get a lot of PUSHBACK from the board.

questions.question: With all due ____, I must completely reject your proposal. (Con el debido respeto).
questions.explanation: With all due respect = Con el debido respeto.

questions.question: You claim that our customers love the new design, but looking at the sales drop, I ____ to differ. (Me permito discrepar).
questions.explanation: I beg to differ = Me permito discrepar.

questions.question: That's a ____ point, but have you considered the legal implications? (Un punto válido).
questions.explanation: That's a valid point, but... = Es un punto válido, pero...

questions.question: I have serious ____ about hiring him. He doesn't seem reliable. (Tengo reservas/dudas).
questions.explanation: I have reservations about = Tengo reservas/dudas sobre...

questions.question: We are never going to convince each other. Let's agree to ____. (Acordemos no estar de acuerdo).
I actually like your idea, but just to play ____'s advocate, what if our competitor copies it? (Abogado del diablo).
questions.explanation: Play devil's advocate = hacer de abogado del diablo.

questions.question: If we propose cutting employee bonuses, expect a massive amount of ____ from the staff. (Resistencia/Rechazo).
I hear what you're saying, but I ____ it from a different perspective. (Lo veo desde otra perspectiva).
questions.explanation: I see it from a different perspective = Lo veo de otro modo.

questions.question: I'm afraid I don't entirely ____ your view on this matter. (No comparto tu visión).
questions.explanation: I don't entirely share your view = No comparto del todo tu opinión.

questions.question: While I ____ your concerns, the decision has already been made. (Aprecio/Entiendo).
questions.explanation: While I appreciate your concerns = Aunque aprecio/entiendo tus preocupaciones.

questions.question: I understand where you're ____ from, but the data says otherwise. (Entiendo de dónde vienes / tu postura).
questions.explanation: I understand where you're coming from = Entiendo tu punto de vista.

questions.question: That is certainly one way of ____ at it. However... (Esa es ciertamente una forma de verlo).
questions.explanation: That is one way of looking at it = Es una forma de verlo (diplomacia pasivo-agresiva).

questions.question: I'm not fully ____ that this is the best course of action. (No estoy totalmente convencido).
questions.explanation: I'm not fully convinced = No estoy del todo convencido.

questions.question: Let's put a ____ in this topic and discuss it later. (Dejemos esto en pausa).
questions.explanation: Put a pin in it = dejar un tema en pausa para más tarde.

questions.question: Let's take this offline. (¿Qué significa esto en una reunión?)
options: Hablemos de esto en privado después
questions.correct_answer: Hablemos de esto en privado después
questions.explanation: Take this offline = hablarlo en privado o fuera de la reunión.

questions.question: I take ____ with your claim that our quality has dropped. (Tengo un problema / Discrepo con...).
questions.explanation: Take issue with = discrepar fuertemente, molestarse por una afirmación.

questions.question: We seem to be talking at ____ purposes. We are misunderstanding each other. (Hablar sin entenderse).
questions.explanation: Talk at cross purposes = hablar de cosas distintas pensando que hablan de lo mismo.

questions.question: I think we're going around in ____. We aren't making any progress. (Dar vueltas en círculo).
questions.explanation: Go around in circles = dar vueltas sobre lo mismo sin avanzar.

questions.question: To be perfectly ____, your proposal is too expensive. (Para ser perfectamente franco).
questions.explanation: To be perfectly frank (o candid) = para ser franco/sincero.

questions.question: Up to a ____, I agree with you, but not entirely. (Hasta cierto punto).
questions.explanation: Up to a point = hasta cierto punto.

questions.question: With all due ____. (Respeto con R)
I ____ to differ. (Me permito con B)
That's a ____ point. (Punto válido con V)
I have ____ about this. (Reservas/dudas con R)
Let's agree to ____. (No estar de acuerdo con D)
Play ____'s advocate. (Abogado del diablo con D)
Expect a lot of ____. (Resistencia/oposición con P)
I don't ____ your view. (Comparto con S)
I see where you're ____ from. (Viniendo con C)
Let's take this ____. (Fuera de la reunión con O)
